Episode 258. The Predator of All Dimensions (12)
-Orgal, did the witch give you an answer?

-[Dammit, no. I relayed your words through the demon trio, but it seems no one can meet the witch right now. Not just me, but even them, the residents of the abyss. It seems they were affected by something in this battle between Malugia and Kelliark.]
A conversation Jin and Orgal had a while ago.

At that time, Jin had asked Orgal to convey to the witch that he wanted to meet her in person. Orgal had only received a reply from the demon trio that it was impossible, but the truth was related to the Origin Stone.
From that time on, Helluram had been preparing to ensure that the completed Origin Stone would not arrive in this 677th dimension in a 'whole state'.
The Demon Army's dimensional gates, still open in the sky, and the complex dimensional passages connected beyond them.
Kelliark had already experienced Malugia and Kragos damaging those paths and appearing on the battlefield.
But now, Helluram was saying not only that the Origin Stone would not arrive on time, but that it would not be whole.

Helluram finally revealing herself and deploying the chaos of the abyss throughout the entire battlefield and its subspaces to engage in a head-on power struggle with Kelliark was her final move for that purpose.

[You wouldn't have been able to pay attention while you were looking into me. But it's too late now. My blood and flesh have already stained your Origin Stone. It has become something different from what you knew.]
The aftermath of Helluram and Kelliark's battle did not only distort the battlefield. It had also affected the path the Origin Stone was on, beyond the dimensional gates, and its very body.
It wasn't for nothing that Kelliark hadn't considered this phenomenon.

He had conquered all dimensions, trampled hundreds of Genesis Knights, subjugated more gods than that, and massacred countless people, but among them, there was no one with an authority comparable to Helluram's.
Besides, Helluram had never once responded to a direct confrontation with him, even at the cost of her very existence being erased by history manipulation.

This was the first time the two beings had clashed, and Kelliark had never once calculated a situation identical to this using the Origin Stone. He had never even hypothesized a situation where he would be battling the Vamel Alliance like this, summon a completed Origin Stone, have Malugia intervene, and even have Helluram's true form appear.
Therefore, Kelliark did not know what could happen as a result of that aftermath.
That if he and Helluram fought with all their might, the interference could even surpass the limits and sufficiently damage the Origin Stone existing within the dimensional passage.
[So now, the method to realize your great ambition rests solely in your hands.]
Gush!

A clot of blood poured from Kelliark's mouth. The cracked skull from Crantel's blow was still visibly white. Soon, he picked up something that had flowed out from between his split skull with his hand, put it back into his head, and looked up at Helluram.
"You hate me very much, witch... I didn't know you and Malugia would trip me up like this."
The completed Origin Stones were not one.
But the only Origin Stone that could break through the interference limit was the one Helluram had touched.
If Malugia hadn't attacked the Demon Army's main base in the Empire, Kelliark might have been able to try summoning one, perhaps even two more, but now the Demon Army no longer had the capacity.
[Like many orphans, you too are misunderstanding. I have no reason to hate orphans. You are no different. I simply came to see you to protect my own foundation.]

"Yes, you must be glad to have those pathetic parents, that Focal or Malugia, the egos of the Sun God. Puhuhu... one of them delays the arrival of the Origin Stone, and another one damages that Origin Stone. And yet another one, in the first place... made me come here in person."
Kelliark turned his head.
It was to see Jin, the very person who had made him decide to visit the 677th dimension himself. Jin was still struggling to hold his position in front of Valeria and Enya.

"Now I understand your expression, Jin Runcandel. Those desperate eyes. Look, Jin. I have seized a power unparalleled in the world, and you, despite being so weak, are somehow blocking me and endlessly renewing miracles. But in the end, we are both in a position to be toyed with by immortals who can read time a little."
There were many reasons why Helluram and Malugia could push Kelliark back now.

Kelliark's hasty visit to the 677th dimension, the Vamel Alliance showing a strength that far surpassed the Demon Army's expectations, Chiron, Van, and the other Genesis Knights showing a surprising performance that shocked even Kelliark, and so on...
But the biggest factor was that Helluram and Malugia had read all the various futures hidden between those events.

If those two hadn't read the future, Kelliark would never have been in such a serious crisis now. He wouldn't have been able to strike the Demon Army's main base in advance, nor could he have damaged the Origin Stone at the optimal time.

"In truth, from a certain point on, I became lukewarm. I couldn't feel whether it was really necessary to conquer time. The dimensions, excluding this place, were weak worlds like dandelion seeds that scatter with just a breath. Maybe that's why, looking back, it doesn't seem like it was that painful to obtain this much power."
Vitality was surging in Kelliark's eyes. Even though he had already experienced death a couple of times.

"Whether I fall, or you fall. At that time, those damn immortals who are greater than time will move to achieve their respective goals of darkness or ruin. If that happens, it will be proven that both you and I were wrong in the end."
Let's just not create that kind of ending.
As Kelliark said that, a silence fell for a while.
The battlefield that had been churning like water momentarily regained its original form, and the rivers that had been raging madly calmed down.
It wasn't that they had stopped fighting foolishly to listen to his story. The Genesis Knights and the immortals had been looking for a chance to strike him the whole time Kelliark was speaking.
There just wasn't one.
Despite being in a more vulnerable state than ever before, Kelliark suddenly seemed to have become a greater being. Soon, he pounded his chest with his fists and shouted at Jin.

"I don't care about the immortals' trivial order. You and I, we just need to determine who was right in the end. I will not change my methods. If the world denies me like this, the more it does, the more cruelly and viciously I will clutch everything in this grasp. I will shake, crush, and mold them with these two hands until they are finally satisfactory to my eyes. Even if I become empty in the end by doing so, I will smile when I remember the joy of today's victory."

Something beyond madness was shining in Kelliark's eyes. Those who saw those eyes momentarily saw the image of Jin in him. They were the eyes that only one who 'never' falls and is never broken can have.
Even Jin recognized it. That right now, Kelliark had a face like his own.

"This is crazy... All of you, get out of this world, even one second faster. The world I remember was not like this. When I set everything right, I will leave too. Before I become a monster like you, before I become a terrible immortal like you all."
Now, your time.
If you endure your time, the curse will be lifted. Jin, conscious of his rotting, stiff, and unmoving left arm, straightened his posture.
The first to move was Malugia.
As she extended her hand towards Kelliark, dozens of huge, golden cubes formed around him. Soon, the cubes struck Kelliark like thunder, but he was no longer there.
In an instant, he was in the sky, behind Helluram, trying to bite her neck. The darkness and chaotic energy spreading like a shield tried to push Kelliark away, but his teeth were already sinking in.
Krrk! A sound no different from chewing human flesh was heard. Kelliark spat out the flesh that filled his mouth and bit her once more.
No scream or groan was heard. But the darkness that had spread everywhere was momentarily blurring. She too had consumed a lot of her authority to deceive Kelliark and defile the Origin Stone.

Puk, puk! By the time the darkness turned into thorns and began to pierce his head, spine, and heart, Kelliark had once again distanced himself from Helluram. In that gap, the swords of the Genesis Knights, Araxion, and Kragos swept Kelliark, and as he fled from them and fell to the ground, he had lost about half of his body.

A figure like a pile of rags rather than a person, a dangling eyeball on his twisted face, and slow regeneration. If Chiron and Van, who were the first to close the distance again, were to tear apart his remaining body with their blows, it seemed he would not be able to stand up again.
But Chiron and Van couldn't swing their swords even though they had secured a clear chance to attack.
'The Flame Orb...!'

The Annihilation Flame Orb. The final chapter of the magic that the darkness had been covering was once again emitting heat. It was tearing through Helluram's darkness and creating a brilliant radiance.

It burned even more intensely than before. Even Chiron and Van were pressed down by its heat, their movements slowing, and even Helluram was hiding her body again in the farthest darkness to escape the light.
No one could go against the heat to strike Kelliark. In that time, Kelliark reconstituted his body and caught his breath.
"Keuhuuk, hook...!"

As soon as he regained a relatively whole form, the heat of the Annihilation Flame Orb rapidly subsided. Kelliark had thrown a gamble to reclaim his greatest remaining offensive means from the witch for the time being.
Helluram could not cover the Annihilation Flame Orb again. Neither could Malugia and Araxion, who had amplified the sun energy of destruction, nor could anyone on the battlefield.
Therefore, those who opposed Kelliark had no choice but to fight with their backs to the sun that was the Annihilation Flame Orb once more.

"Even without the Origin Stone, I am Kelliark Zipple. The strongest being in all dimensions. But Helluram, you only said the Origin Stone was damaged, you didn't say it couldn't arrive. Huhu, if it's different, there will be a certain taste in using it as it is."
Soon, Kelliark's gaze reached Laprarosa.
He was still most wary of Jin entering Solderet's legacy.
